after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Consider the plane curve $\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy).$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & =\operatorname{sin}⁡xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡xy$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(0,\frac{\pi }{2})$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(0,\frac{\pi }{2})={f}_{y}(0,\frac{\pi }{2})i-{f}_{x}(0,\frac{\pi }{2})j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(0,\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))\,j \\  & =(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))i-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))\,j \\ t(0,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{cos}⁡(0\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}))i-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}))j \\  & =-i+\frac{\pi }{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $-i+\frac{\pi }{2}\,j.$

decision.explanation: For f(x,y)=2xy-3x²+y, a tangent vector is (2x+1,6x-2y). Perpendicularity to j requires 6x-2y=0, so y=3x. Substitution into the curve gives 3x(x+1)=0, yielding (0,0) and (-1,-3). The tangent vectors at both points are nonzero.

after.problem: At which points on the curve $2xy-3{x}^{2}=-y$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3{x}^{2}=-y \\ 2xy-3{x}^{2}+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2xy-3{x}^{2}+y$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy-3{x}^{2}+y)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy-3{x}^{2}+y)j \\  & =(2x+1)\,i-2(y-3x)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j & =0 \\ ((2x+1)\,i-2(y-3x)\,j)\cdot j & =0 \\ -2(y-3x) & =0 \\ y & =3x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=3x$ into the equation of our curve gives:  

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3{x}^{2}+y & =0 \\ 2x(3x)-3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 3x(x+1) & =0 \\ x & =0\,\text{or}\,x=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

- If $x=0$, we get $y=0$ and the corresponding point is $(0,0).$

- If $x=-1$, we get $y=-3$ and the corresponding point is $(-1,-3).$

At which points on the curve 2xy−3x2=−y is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector j?

a
(0,3) and (0,−3)
b
(3,0) and (−1,0)
c
(0,1) and (1,−3)
d
(0,0) and (−1,−3)
e
(0,−1) and (0,−3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side: 2xy−3x2=−y2xy−3x2+y=0

If we set f(x,y)=2xy−3x2+y, our curve can be viewed as the level curve f(x,y)=0.

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows: t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j

So, we calculate t(x,y):

t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j=∂∂y(2xy−3x2+y)i−∂∂x(2xy−3x2+y)j=(2x+1)i−2(y−3x)j

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to j, we must have t⋅j=0.

t(x,y)⋅j=0((2x+1)i−2(y−3x)j)⋅j=0−2(y−3x)=0y=3x

Substituting y=3x into the equation of our curve gives:

2xy−3x2+y=02x(3x)−3x2+3x=06x2−3x2+3x=03x2+3x=03x(x+1)=0x=0orx=−1

Finally:

  • If x=0, we get y=0 and the corresponding point is (0,0).

  • If x=−1, we get y=−3 and the corresponding point is (−1,−3).

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Points on a Curve at which the Tangent Vector is Perpendicular to a Given Vector
content.problem: At which points on the curve $2xy-3{x}^{2}=-y$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3{x}^{2}=-y \\ 2xy-3{x}^{2}+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2xy-3{x}^{2}+y$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy-3{x}^{2}+y)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy-3{x}^{2}+y)j \\  & =(2x+1)\,i-2(y-3x)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j & =0 \\ ((2x+1)\,i-2(y-3x)\,j)\cdot j & =0 \\ -2(y-3x) & =0 \\ y & =3x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=3x$ into the equation of our curve gives:  

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3{x}^{2}+y & =0 \\ 2x(3x)-3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 3x(x+1) & =0 \\ x & =0\,\text{or}\,x=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

- If $x=0$, we get $y=0$ and the corresponding point is $(0,0).$

- If $x=-1$, we get $y=-3$ and the corresponding point is $(-1,-3).$

$$

$$

$$

$$

content.problem: Consider the plane curve $xy=3-{x}^{2}-{y}^{3}.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(-1,-1).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}xy & =3-{x}^{2}-{y}^{3} \\ xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{3} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{3},$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=3.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(-1,-1)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(-1,-1)={f}_{y}(-1,-1)i-{f}_{x}(-1,-1)j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{3})i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{3})j \\  & =(x+3{y}^{2})i-(y+2x)j \\ t(-1,-1) & =(-1+3(-1)^{2})i-(-1+2(-1))j \\  & =2\,i+3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $2\,i+3\,j.$
